title: Let AI Help You Build Relationships, but Don’t Let It Communicate for You
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership argues that AI is useful for the logistics of relationship-building but corrosive when it writes the messages themselves. Most leaders intend to stay connected, yet the pressure of the day pulls attention away and relationships drift. The piece says AI can compile the list of relationships that matter, keep background notes, track contact, and flag who has not heard from you lately. The danger is that an AI draft arrives in seconds and reads better than anything a busy leader would write, so outreach becomes a task to check off. The authors answer that people judge a message by the effort they believe went into it, and that the cost of an inauthentic note stays hidden because people quietly invest less in return. Their conclusion is that leaders should use every tool to know who needs to hear from them and then show up themselves.
points: The essay divides the work cleanly: AI handles memory, prompting, and tracking, while the leader keeps the voice and the decision about what to say.
Polish is a false signal, since people read effort and personal detail as evidence that a human is behind the message.
The cost of a hollow message is hidden because few people say so; they simply invest a little less in the relationship.
Specific details only you would know and a curious follow-up question are the markers that make outreach land as care.
The hard part of outreach, deciding what to say, is the point of the exercise and should not be outsourced.
quotes: AI can help leaders keep the relationship focus they want, as long as they give it the right job.
It can surface who hasn’t heard from you recently, flag a moment worth acknowledging, and remind you why a particular person deserves your attention now.
But the moment AI starts writing the messages, the value of the relationship collapses.
People judge a message by the effort they believe went into it, not by its finish.
The cost of an inauthentic message stays hidden. Few people tell a leader that a message felt hollow. They simply invest a little less in return.
Steady outreach only lands as care when the person on the other end sees evidence of a human being.
The leaders who build the strongest relationships keep the human part for themselves. They use every tool available to know who needs to hear from them. Then they show up themselves.
